# No nonzero positive raw-response square can be a minorant of full V

STATUS: ANALYTIC_PAPER_CANDIDATE, independent review pending.
Base: a9f89af4dea01430be79ed3d2499afaac94e2b71.
Original full V and RH: OPEN. No negative original-V witness is claimed.

## F0. Return point and exact decision effect

The old SOURCE_ENERGY_PREFLIGHT excludes a bounded reservoir with specified
unitary dynamics. NULLFIELD excludes a positive fraction of a specified lifted
field energy. POINCARECOMP excludes an absolute derivative comparison. None
may be generalized just by dropping its hypotheses. Here a direct corollary
of the accepted source-tail estimate and analytic positivity propagation
excludes an entire precisely stated class of minorants of ORIGINAL V.

The class consists of a fixed nonnegative weighted square of the raw scalar
response P_c(t)=sum_i c_i f(t+x_i). This includes ordinary L2 energy, bounded
nonnegative weights and individual point observations. It does not cover a
different transformed response, a source-dependent moving observation, or a
weight that changes with the tested family. The mathematical mechanism is
inherited tail comparison plus all-rank propagation, not a new source identity
or a new positivity mechanism. No literature-novelty claim is made.

Pinned inputs: ANALYTIC_POSITIVITY_PROPAGATION A1--A2; FULL_SIGN_TRANSFER_AUDIT
for the unchanged source/target; SOURCE_ENERGY_PREFLIGHT E7 for the full-source
tail estimate; NULLFIELD_INTAKE_AND_COUPLING I2--I3 for prior-scope comparison;
LAYER_GRAM_TEST L2--L5 for the positive quartic comparison below.

## F1. Fixed target, observation measures and theorem

Let f=Phi/||Phi||_2 be the complete positive even theta source and

    V(x,y)=int_0^infinity (2t+x+y) f(t+x)f(t+y)dt.

Let mu be a nonzero, positive, locally finite Borel measure on [0,infinity)
such that, for every a>0,

    int_[0,infinity) exp(-a exp(2t)) dmu(t)<infinity.       (F1)

Finite measures, Lebesgue measure and measures with polynomially growing
densities satisfy F1. In particular atoms, including an atom at zero, are
allowed. Define the raw-response Gram kernel

    G_mu(x,y)=int_[0,infinity) f(t+x)f(t+y) dmu(t),
    G_mu[c]=int |P_c(t)|^2 dmu(t)>=0.                     (F2)

Claim: for EVERY such mu, every kappa>0 and every nonempty open real interval J,
there is a finite complex row with nodes in J for which

    V[c] < kappa G_mu[c], with G_mu[c]>0.                 (F3)

In particular J can be the original I=(-log(2)/2,0). Equivalently, no positive
constant multiple of this fixed nonzero raw-response Gram kernel is a PSD
minorant of V on the entire required finite-family class. This is a statement
about a lower-bound strategy, not about the sign of V itself.

## F2. The full kernels have one common holomorphic domain

The accepted full-series bound on S={z:|Im z|<pi/4} says that, for z in a
fixed compact subset and t>=0,

    |f(z+t)| <= C exp(9t/2) exp(-c exp(2t)), c>0.          (F4)

For a pair of compacts the product is bounded by C' exp(-c' exp(2t)),
absorbing exp(9t) into part of the exponential. F1 therefore provides an
integrable majorant for G_mu on every compact of S x S. The integrals over
bounded t intervals are holomorphic, and their tails converge uniformly on
compacts. Thus G_mu is jointly holomorphic on S x S. V has exactly that
extension by accepted A2. K_kappa=V-kappa G_mu is consequently holomorphic
there and real symmetric on real nodes. No continuation of mu itself is used.

## F3. A distant negative diagonal of the COMPARISON kernel

Full-source E7 proves, for u>=1,

    f'(u)<=-pi exp(2u) f(u).

For R>=1 put L_R=pi exp(2R). Integrating the differential inequality gives
f(R+s)<=f(R) exp(-L_R s) for s>=0. Exact evenness, then this bound, gives

    V(-R,-R)=2 int_R^infinity u f(u)^2 du
      <= f(R)^2 [R/L_R+1/(2 L_R^2)].                     (F5)

Since mu is nonzero and locally finite, some finite B>=0 has
m=mu([0,B]) in (0,infinity). If R>B+1, evenness and the decreasing positive
tail imply f(t-R)=f(R-t)>=f(R) for 0<=t<=B. Hence

    G_mu(-R,-R)>=m f(R)^2.                              (F6)

This includes mu concentrated at t=0. The quotient in F5--F6 tends to zero:

    0<V(-R,-R)/G_mu(-R,-R)
       <=[R/L_R+1/(2 L_R^2)]/m ->0.                     (F7)

For each fixed kappa, sufficiently large R therefore gives
K_kappa(-R,-R)<0. Both diagonal values themselves are positive; the negative
quantity here is V-kappa G_mu, not V. No divergent endpoint test is used.

## F4. Localization to the ORIGINAL allowed interval and normalization

If K_kappa were PSD on every finite complex row in J, the accepted analytic
propagation lemma A1 would make it PSD on all of R. Its hypotheses are
verified in F2, and the mixed old/new matrices in that lemma are essential.
This contradicts F7. Thus some finite row c in J has K_kappa[c]<0.

To ensure G_mu[c]>0 without an unstated injectivity assumption, handle the
possible case G_mu[c]=0 explicitly. Choose a node a in J and let e be its
one-node row. Because f is strictly positive and mu nonzero, G_mu[e]>0.
The Gram identity gives P_c=0 mu-almost everywhere, so
G_mu[c+epsilon e]=epsilon^2 G_mu[e]>0 for real epsilon!=0.
The finite quadratic expression K_kappa[c+epsilon e] remains negative for
sufficiently small epsilon by continuity. Adjoin a to the row if needed.
This proves F3, including atomic measures and possible null Gram rows.

Rescale such a row to G_mu[c]=1. Consequently, on any J,

    inf_{finite rows, G_mu[c]>0} V[c]/G_mu[c] <= 0.        (F8)

IF the still-open V>=0 is true, this infimum is exactly zero. Without that
hypothesis we assert only the upper bound, not equality or a negative V.
The proof gives no rank, coefficient-size or conditioning bound for the
localized rows. Positive fixed-rank tests are not contradicted.

## F5. Consequence for exact energy realizations

Any representation V= kappa G_mu + R with R a PSD kernel on all rows is
excluded by F3. In particular, if an exact Hilbert Gram family Psi_x for V
were constructed, its raw scalar readout cannot be bounded: there cannot
be a bounded linear operator B into L2(mu) with

    (B Psi_x)(t)=f(t+x), for every x in J.                (F9)

Indeed G_mu[c]<=||B||^2 V[c] would contradict F3 with kappa=1/||B||^2.
B cannot have norm zero because every individual readout is nonzero.
For mu=delta_T, this rules out a bounded vector readout of f(T+x), T>=0,
without assuming any particular generator, evolution or reservoir dynamics.
Unbounded observations, other transformed fields, and exact cancellations
are outside this implication. Their existence or positivity is not supplied.

This does NOT prohibit all positive Gram representations. The accepted
quartic source f_q(u)=C exp(-a u^4-bu^2), a>0, has an explicit positive
Gram representation for V_q (LAYER_GRAM_TEST L2--L5), yet its decreasing
tail satisfies -f_q'/f_q=4au^3+2bu and V_q(-R,-R)/f_q(R)^2->0.
The same comparison argument applies to it for mu=delta_0; we do not
import the entire F1 measure class for the quartic source. Thus ordinary
positivity and absence of a raw point-readout floor are compatible. Conversely, the
Gaussian f_g(u)=C exp(-bu^2), b>0, has exactly
V_g(x,y)=f_g(x)f_g(y)/(2b), allowing a delta_0 floor. Its slope grows only
linearly; the crucial ratio R/L_R does not tend to zero there.

Decision: do not propose another fixed nonnegative weighted raw-response
square as an independently positive part of V, even with an arbitrarily
small constant. A useful remaining construction must respect F9's
observation obstruction and still prove its exact identity with full V.
This is a broader filter from old analytic tools, not an RH proof, an
original-source negative witness, a canonical admission or a counter reset.

AUTOPSY: dropped=OBJECT_IDENTITY; note=Every fixed nonzero admissible positive measure of raw-response squares has more diagonal mass than original V can pay after translation; analytic all-rank propagation excludes a positive floor already on the original interval.

# Independent review: no fixed raw-response norm floor

**Verdict: ACCEPT_FIXED_POSITIVE_RAW_RESPONSE_MINORANT_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.**

Final candidate `RAW_RESPONSE_FLOOR_CANDIDATE.md`, SHA256 `8a5a91813d3b8b7a6c8e21c439c7436358b1e1989818db2405fb414992ce4260` (8030 bytes, 158 LF), was read completely. The final manifest `RAW_RESPONSE_FLOOR_PINS.json` has SHA256 `299e97d554730285ffa7c11bf6ef70eb79870c3f6dda53cbeb50d2397e6cbbd1`. All claims F0–F5, including equations F1–F9, are accepted with the stated scope. No mathematical correction remains after the quartic qualification described below.

The theorem is the universal comparison obstruction for each fixed nonzero positive locally finite measure satisfying F1, every positive constant, and every nonempty open real node interval. It does not assert that original V has a negative row or that all Gram representations are impossible.

## 1. Exact inputs and correction from the first draft

All source hashes were checked in the isolated research checkout:

| Project input | SHA256 |
|---|---|
| REPORT_2026-09-13_ANALYTIC_POSITIVITY_PROPAGATION.md | fb83c216aef4687425074732904f9d2f52aac77527a926e7556fb0067335e2bd |
| REPORT_2026-09-12_FULL_SIGN_TRANSFER_AUDIT.md | 1e296a504631b58beb7863f4c7f36174bd08876cfc7093febfe00cc8306a5282 |
| REPORT_2026-09-13_SOURCE_ENERGY_PREFLIGHT.md | e2b168250777bc13e6ba740af7e977ebf7807b8b7170f089c711d32a1dd83307 |
| REPORT_2026-09-15_NULLFIELD_INTAKE_AND_COUPLING.md | f93a8806c4e4e899342ce5318b788ee2e79c9edc2bad7b1a634bc3ac8423a35a |
| REPORT_2026-09-15_LAYER_GRAM_TEST.md | a402aa67f81824945d3324881e2a822a8e897a07316b3dc780e671228715e1eb |
| orchestrator/state/CHANNEL_RUNTIME.json | f7bb8eed28bf9b67292f67bbbdde96cecb4baf42e758e0acbb4be34d5baa6418 |

The named mathematical sections were read directly: analytic propagation A1–A2, including mixed old/new blocks; full-sign source/target sections 1–2 and 7; source-energy E7 and its bounded-reservoir scope; NULLFIELD I2–I3; and layer-Gram L2–L5. Their recorded prior acceptance is inherited. No new audit of the entire classical Weil chain or source-sign proof is asserted. The runtime hash is provenance, not a proof premise or fresh authorization.

The first draft's phrase applying the same comparison to the quartic source needed an explicit measure restriction. For example, dmu(t)=exp(t^5)dt is locally finite and satisfies F1 for every a>0, because exp(2t) eventually dominates t^5. But it makes quartic-response squared integrals divergent. Final F5 now restricts that comparison to mu=delta_0 and explicitly declines to import the full F1 class. This resolves the only identified scope defect; the theta theorem did not require a change.

## 2. Measure class and common holomorphic domain

Positive local finiteness on [0,infinity) implies sigma-finiteness by the compact exhaustion [0,n]. No absolute continuity or atom-free assumption is used. The examples in F1 are valid, including an atom at zero. Since the measure is nonzero, at least one compact [0,B] has positive finite mass; otherwise countable exhaustion would make the entire measure zero.

For compacts in S={|Im z|<pi/4}, the full-series envelope in accepted A2 applies to every t>=0. Multiplying two such envelopes gives at most C exp(9t)exp(-c exp(2t)); the polynomial-in-exp(t) factor can be absorbed into a smaller positive c. F1, which holds for every positive coefficient, consequently pays one integrable majorant for each compact pair. The coefficient may become small for far negative real shifts, so the universal quantifier in F1 is useful and is not replaced by a single moment assumption.

On bounded observation intervals the measure is finite and the integrand is holomorphic and uniformly bounded on compacts. These truncated parameter integrals are holomorphic. The common integrable tail majorant gives locally uniform convergence to G_mu on S x S, establishing its joint holomorphic extension, including for atomic measures. The accepted V extension is on that same product domain. Thus K=V-kappa G_mu has all the analyticity and real-symmetry hypotheses required for all-rank propagation. The source is not truncated and no analytic continuation of the measure is presumed.

For every finite row, each shifted source is in L2(mu) by this domination. Therefore the finite Gram expansion is legitimate and G_mu[c]=integral |P_c|^2. Every one-node diagonal is finite and strictly positive since f is strictly positive at every real argument and mu is nonzero. F1 is a stated sufficient measure condition; the theorem does not claim it characterizes every possible admissible observation measure.

## 3. Full-source tail ratio and distant comparison diagonal

E7's bound is an actual full-series inequality. For u>=1, each positive mode has logarithmic derivative

    9/2 +6/(2q_n-3)-2q_n <=-q_n,
    q_n=pi n^2 exp(2u).

Uniformly convergent differentiated mode sums permit summation, and q_n>=pi exp(2u) gives f'(u)<=-pi exp(2u)f(u). Integrating the logarithmic inequality yields

    f(R+s)/f(R)<=exp[-integral_R^(R+s) pi exp(2u)du]
                 <=exp(-L_R s),  L_R=pi exp(2R).

Evenness of the complete original source gives V(-R,-R)=2 integral_R^infinity u f(u)^2 du. Consequently

    V(-R,-R)/f(R)^2
      <=2 integral_0^infinity (R+s)exp(-2L_R s)ds
      =R/L_R+1/(2L_R^2),

with the factor 2 and squared-tail exponent intact. This tends to zero; it is stronger than merely V(-R,-R) tending to zero.

For the compact mass m=mu([0,B])>0, choose R>B+1. Then R-t>=1 for 0<=t<=B. Tail monotonicity and evenness give f(t-R)=f(R-t)>=f(R). Integrating that lower bound gives G_mu(-R,-R)>=m f(R)^2. This remains valid if all mass lies at zero. Both diagonals remain finite and positive, while their ratio tends to zero as in F7. Hence every fixed kappa>0 eventually gives a strictly negative comparison diagonal K(-R,-R). It is only K that is negative; no negative original V diagonal occurs.

## 4. Localization, possible null rows and exact quantifiers

Assume the same fixed K is PSD on every finite complex row in a nonempty open interval J. The accepted propagation lemma applies with global real interval R and product neighborhood S x S. It extends all finite PSD matrices to every real node set, including -R, contradicting the preceding diagonal. Its use preserves mixed old/new matrices through finite differences and ordered Taylor limits; no fixed-rank or solely diagonal hypothesis would justify this step. The contradiction yields some finite row in J with K[c]<0, without a rank or conditioning estimate.

If this row has G_mu[c]=0, its actual response vanishes mu-almost everywhere. Adjoin any one-node row e at a in J, combining duplicate nodes when needed. G_mu[e]>0. Since the old response is zero almost everywhere, all Gram cross terms vanish and, for nonzero real epsilon,

    G_mu[c+epsilon e]=epsilon^2 G_mu[e]>0.

The finite quadratic expression K[c+epsilon e] is continuous in epsilon and retains its strict negative sign for sufficiently small epsilon. Thus the claimed positive-denominator witness always exists, even for rank-one atomic Gram kernels or other large null spaces. No synthesis injectivity is silently assumed.

This proves the order of quantifiers in F3: fix mu, kappa and J, then obtain a finite row depending on them. Homogeneous rescaling makes G_mu[c]=1. Having ratios below every positive kappa proves only inf V[c]/G_mu[c]<=0. If V is nonnegative on all rows, the infimum is zero; without that unproved hypothesis equality is not claimed. A measure chosen from source information but fixed throughout the tests remains within the theorem; row-dependent measures and moving observations do not.

## 5. Conditional readout obstruction

If V were represented exactly by Hilbert vectors Psi_x on J and a bounded linear B satisfied B Psi_x=f(.+x) in L2(mu), finite linearity would give

    G_mu[c]=||B sum c_i Psi_(x_i)||^2
            <=||B||^2 ||sum c_i Psi_(x_i)||^2
            =||B||^2 V[c].

The norm of B is nonzero because every single readout is nonzero. Taking kappa=1/||B||^2 contradicts F3. This implication requires only the hypothetical exact Gram identity and bounded readout, not an assumed generator, dynamics, or continuation of the Hilbert vectors outside J. For delta_T, L2(mu) is the one-dimensional observation space, so it also excludes a bounded linear functional, equivalently a fixed Hilbert-vector readout, at any fixed T>=0.

This is broader than the specified old bounded-reservoir exclusion because those evolution assumptions are unnecessary here. The separate NULLFIELD theorem concerned a particular primitive/derivative lifted energy, not this raw-response measure class; it is retained as a prior-scope comparison and is not generalized by deleting its hypotheses. Unbounded readouts, different transformed fields, exact cancellations, or row-dependent observation laws are outside F9. None is constructed by this result.

## 6. Quartic and Gaussian controls; final scope

The pinned quartic construction covers C>0, a>0 and real b, and explicitly realizes the integrated V_q through positive monomial features at every rank. For large R its logarithmic slope 4aR^3+2bR is positive and eventually increasing. One may for example bound the slope below by 2aR^3 throughout u>=R for sufficiently large R. The same tail integration then gives V_q(-R,-R)/f_q(R)^2 tending to zero. For mu=delta_0 the raw kernel is simply the entire product f_q(z)f_q(w), while V_q has the common analytic domain from its quartic decay. Analytic localization therefore proves the point-readout floor obstruction despite the known positive Gram representation. The final measure qualification is essential and correct.

For the Gaussian, differentiating the product f_g(t+x)f_g(t+y) integrates the original kernel exactly to f_g(x)f_g(y)/(2b). Hence G_delta0 is a genuine positive floor with kappa=1/(2b). Its tail slope is 2bR, and R/L_R does not vanish. Thus this control tests precisely the superlinear-slope step, not a supposed universal obstruction for all positive even sources.

The final conclusion is an honest corollary of old full-tail and propagation tools. It rules out every fixed nonzero positive raw-response square in the stated class as a positive minorant of original V, even with arbitrarily small fixed coefficient. It does not rule out all Gram representations, identify the sign of V, create a negative theta row, add a new source identity, or prove/disprove RH. Canonical observation-only HOLD, source-sign counters and all other files remain untouched. Only this assigned private review file was written; no descendants, external dispatch, commit, push or branch creation was performed.

# Parent check: raw-response square minorants

Verdict: ACCEPT_FIXED_POSITIVE_RAW_RESPONSE_MINORANT_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.
The complete final independent review was read; the quartic delta_0 scope correction is incorporated below.
Review SHA256: 1353f3af063d7b20844fc9d537b72612fb7861f55c51ded3b8dbdd2c0ef67d36. Final candidate SHA256:
8a5a91813d3b8b7a6c8e21c439c7436358b1e1989818db2405fb414992ce4260.

The parent read the full candidate and exact old input formulas. The original
V, normalization, physical t>=0 cutoff and all-finite complex quantifier are
unchanged. This is a corollary/filter using old source E7 and propagation A1,
not a new source identity, literature discovery or sign supplier.

1. Observation class and holomorphy. F1 for every a>0 makes the product
   full-strip bound integrable for every compact pair. A polynomial factor
   exp(9t) is absorbed by reducing the positive double-exponential rate.
   Local finiteness pays bounded intervals, including an atom at zero.
   Dominated compact tails yield joint holomorphy of G_mu on the same S x S
   as V; no analytic dependence of the measure is being assumed. A measure
   allowed only for selected real shifts would not suffice for this argument.

2. Distant comparison. Source E7 is an inequality for the complete positive
   theta series at u>=1. With L_R=pi exp(2R), it gives f(R+s)<=f(R)e^(-L_R s).
   Direct integration of 2(R+s)e^(-2 L_R s) gives R/L_R+1/(2 L_R^2).
   Evenness is used before that bound, retaining exact cancellation in V.
   Nonzero local finite mu has a finite bounded interval with mass m>0.
   For R>B+1 its entire interval is in the decreasing source tail, and
   f(t-R)=f(R-t)>=f(R). Thus G_mu(-R,-R)>=m f(R)^2.
   This argument includes delta_0 and does not require a positive Lebesgue
   density, an interval of positive support, a total finite mass, or a
   signal-dependent measure. The bound on V/G_mu tends to zero.

3. Full-rank localization. K=V-kappa G_mu has the verified common product
   domain and Hermitian real restriction. If all finite complex matrices
   in J were PSD, accepted A1 would propagate all mixed old/new matrices
   to the far node. Its negative diagonal contradicts that conclusion.
   This is the same accepted analytical mechanism used in old NULLFIELD,
   now with a different precisely specified entire class of observation
   measures. It does not locate a small-rank numerical row in J.

4. Possible null Gram rows. A negative K row could a priori have G_mu=0,
   especially for atomic measures. Adding epsilon times one original column
   gives positive G_mu=epsilon^2 G_mu[e], because the initial response is
   zero mu-almost everywhere. Continuity of the finite quadratic K preserves
   its negative value for small epsilon. Normalization is therefore legal.
   No injectivity of an observation map is assumed. Infimum <=0 follows;
   equality to zero is conditional on the still-open V>=0.

5. Bounded observation consequence. For any presumed Gram family Psi_x,
   a bounded B realizing f(t+x) in L2(mu) would give
   G_mu[c]<=||B||^2 V[c] for every finite row. Since ||B||>0, F3 contradicts
   this. Neither a semigroup nor a particular differential generator is
   required. The assertion does not construct such a Gram family, rule out
   unbounded observations, or show another response is the right one.

6. Comparisons and one necessary scope clarification. Gaussian V equals
   f(x)f(y)/(2b), so it permits a delta_0 floor; its tail has R/L_R constant.
   For the already positive quartic V, eventually L_R=4aR^3+2bR is positive
   and increasing, hence R/L_R->0 and the same delta_0 floor is impossible.
   This demonstrates compatibility of positive V with the obstruction.
   APPLIED AND INDEPENDENTLY CHECKED CLARIFICATION: the quartic comparison is for mu=delta_0,
   not for every F1 measure, since F1 allows measures growing too quickly
   for quartic integrability. The exact theta theorem needs no correction.

No numerical sweep, source truncation, Lean claim, full-V negative witness,
new positive source result, canonical admission or counter reset follows.

AUTOPSY: dropped=OBJECT_IDENTITY; note=The original V cannot pay a fixed nonzero admissible raw-response square; the positive quartic comparator shows that this obstruction is not a negative-sign theorem.
